title: Proactive Model Adaptation Against Concept Drift for Online Time Series Forecasting

problem.claim: Online time series forecasting suffers declining model performance as data distributions evolve through concept drift.

gap.claim: Existing online learning methods overlook the delayed availability of future ground-truth values, creating a temporal gap that can cause adaptation to outdated concepts.

contributions.claim: The paper presents Proceed, a proactive model adaptation framework for online time series forecasting.
Proceed estimates drift between recently used training samples and the current test sample, then translates the estimated drift into parameter adjustments.
Proceed is trained on synthetic diverse concept drifts to enhance generalization.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe Proceed as a novel proactive model adaptation framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on five real-world datasets and various forecast models reportedly show that Proceed improves performance more than state-of-the-art online learning methods.
The authors report that Proceed significantly facilitates forecast-model resilience against concept drift.
Code is reported as available in the linked repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Concept drift causes declining performance in online time series forecasting.
Existing methods continually update model parameters using recent observations and forecasting feedback.
Delayed future ground truth creates a temporal gap and can lead models to adapt to outdated concepts.
Proceed estimates drift relative to the current test sample and proactively adjusts model parameters, using synthetic diverse drifts for training.
The authors report improvements over state-of-the-art online learning methods across five real-world datasets and various forecast models.

source_observation.claim: A delay between observing a sample and obtaining its future ground truth can create a temporal gap between training and testing.

interpretation.claim: Online adaptation may respond to stale concepts when feedback arrives after the forecast horizon.

application.claim: For delayed-feedback forecasting systems, estimate drift relative to the current test sample before updating model parameters.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy applies beyond the described online time series forecasting setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the five real-world datasets.
The abstract does not specify forecast horizons, evaluation metrics, model configurations, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the synthetic drift-generation procedure or adaptation-generator architecture.
